questions.question_text: Each of the following agents have been used to provoke panic attacks in experimental studies except: Choose one answer.
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide, sodium lactate, sodium bicarbonate, yohimbine, m-chlorophenylpiperazine (mCPP), flumazenil, cholecystokinin & caffeine have all been used to induce panic attacks.

questions.question_text: To satisfy criteria for the diagnosis of OCD, a patient would have which ONE of the following? Choose one answer.
questions.explanation: ICD 10 criteria for OCD includes repetitive, intrusive, egodystonic thoughts which are almost impossible to resist and it has an impact on day to day functioning.

questions.question_text: Social phobias are most associated with which ONE of the following? Choose one answer.
questions.explanation: ICD 10 criteria for phobias includes marked fear, or an avoidance of the situation causing phobia.

questions.question_text: Alcohol abuse is most commonly associated with which ONE of the following anxiety disorders? Choose one answer.
questions.explanation: The two anxiety disorders closely tied to alcoholism are panic disorder and social phobia. Comorbid anxiety also makes the outcome of alcoholism poor.

questions.question_text: Agorophobia is NOT considered to be a fear of: Choose one answer.

options.text: Being in crowds and public places
Travelling alone in trains, buses or planes

questions.explanation: It is a fairly well-defined cluster of phobias embracing fears of leaving home, entering shops, crowds and public places, or travelling alone in trains, buses or planes.

questions.question_text: Obsessive compulsive disorder is associated with many neurological conditions including which ONE of the following? Choose one answer.
questions.explanation: OCD is also associated with Gilles de la Tourette's syndrome and encephalitis lethargica.

questions.question_text: An exaggerated startle response is seen in which ONE of the following conditions? Choose one answer.
questions.explanation: Symptoms of hyperarousal seen in PTSD include hypervigilance, exaggerated startle response, irritability...

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is the most common psychiatric disorder in anankastic personality? Choose one answer.
questions.explanation: Depression is more common in patients of anakastic personality disorder. OCD is associated in less than a quarter patients.

questions.question_text: Magical undoing refers to a psychodynamic defence mechanism. It is most commonly associated with which ONE of the following? Choose one answer.
questions.explanation: It is a psychodynamic explanation for OCD symptoms. Magical undoing/thinking refers to omnipotence of thought where persons believe that they can cause an event to occur merely by thinking...

questions.question_text: During a final exam, a worried college student suddenly experiences perioral tingling, carpo-pedal spasms, and feelings of derealization. The most likely diagnosis is: Choose one answer.
questions.explanation: Hyperventilation is a central feature of panic disorder and acute anxiety attacks ... circumoral tingling, carpopedal spasm, and paresthesias are symptoms of tetany.

questions.question_text: Social phobia is more likely to impair functioning in which ONE of the following settings? Choose one answer.
questions.explanation: Presence of 3-4 people makes anxiety higher than a larger group as chances of scrutiny and embarrassment are more in smaller groups.

questions.question_text: Apart from OCD, compulsive acts are also seen in which ONE of the following conditions? Choose one answer.
questions.explanation: Frontal lesions can produce compulsive behavior without obsessions. This supports the theory that OCD has an organic basis.

questions.question_text: A patient with recurrent panic attacks is LEAST likely to develop which ONE of the following? Choose one answer.
questions.explanation: OCD does not share the common feature of panic attacks seen in other anxiety disorders. Recurrent panic attacks can lead to alcohol use...

questions.question_text: A 28 yr. old typist pays 6 pounds-a-day for parking as she is terrified by the thought of being trapped in the hospital underground parking. The most likely diagnosis is: Choose one answer.
questions.explanation: This lady has a specific fear, avoidance and secondary impairment characteristic of phobias.

questions.question_text: Agoraphobia is more frequent while travelling in trains than cars. Which ONE of the following statements explains this? Choose one answer.

options.text: There are more people who can help in a train.
The inescapable nature of the situation.
It is easier to escape from a train.
Agoraphobics are from higher socioeconomic class.
Road traffic accidents can cause agoraphobia.

correct_answer.text: The inescapable nature of the situation.

correct_answers.text: The inescapable nature of the situation.

questions.explanation: Agoraphobia depends on the inescapable nature of a situation – it is easier to escape from a car than train.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following anxiety disorders has the earliest age of onset? Choose one answer
questions.explanation: Social phobias often begin at adolescence. Panic disorders can present at any age but has two peaks of onset, the larger at around 15-25, and a later peak at 45-54. 15-35 is the first peak for agoraphobia, with 45-54 the second peak (very similar to panic disorders)

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following anxiety disorders is LEAST common in women presenting to primary care.
questions.explanation: Most neurotic disorders, except social phobia, are more common in women. Although men and women with social phobia seek treatment in relatively equal numbers, epidemiological studies suggest that men are more likely than women to have social phobia. In agoraphobia, extensive avoidance is more common in females, leading to disparity in clinical presentation - more men with agoraphobia do not seek help. Absence of panic attacks could also reduce help-seeking in men.

questions.question_text: The anxiety disorder with the highest prevalence according to the National Psychiatric Morbidity household survey is: Choose one answer.
questions.explanation: As per the NPM, phobic disorders are the most prevalent. Phobic disorders had a prevalence of 11.9, GAD of 4.5, OCD of 1.6, and panic disorder of 1.0.

questions.question_text: In the treatment of OCD, NICE recommends AGAINST the use of all the following medications EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: NICE recommends the use of SSRIs in cases of moderate or severe OCD. NICE has also provided a list of drugs not recommended for OCD, which include TCAs (except Clomipramine), SNRIs (including venlafaxine), and anxiolytics.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following interventions has no therapeutic value in PTSD?
questions.explanation: A Cochrane review clearly states that routine debriefing after trauma is of no use. Psychological debriefing is either equivalent to, or worse than control or educational interventions in preventing or reducing the severity of PTSD, depression, anxiety and general psychological morbidity after trauma.

questions.question_text: In the treatment of PTSD, there is no RCT evidence regarding the efficacy of which ONE of the following?
questions.explanation: There are RCTs which provide evidence for the efficacy of Mitrazapine, Paroxetine, Imipramine & Phenelzine, and RCTs that provide evidence for non-efficacy of Venlafaxine, Olanzapine, Fluoxetine & Sertraline, but none for Carbamazepine.

questions.question_text: The NICE guidelines for PTSD recommends Mirtazapine or Paroxetine in which ONE of the following circumstances?

options.text: Treatment to be initiated in secondary care
For treatment of treatment resistant PTSD

questions.explanation: Drug treatments (paroxetine or mirtazapine for general use, and amitriptyline or phenelzine for initiation only by mental health specialists) should be considered for the treatment of PTSD in adults who express a preference not to engage in trauma-focused psychological treatment. NICE recommends that trauma-focused interventions (trauma-focused CBT or EMDR) should be first line treatments.

questions.question_text: Assessment for cognitive behavioural therapy in OCD involves all of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: Assessment of the patients' readiness to change
Knowledge of the degree of family involvement
Context in which Obsessions and compulsions have developed
Forensic assessment of intrusive thoughts & impulses

correct_answer.text: Forensic assessment of intrusive thoughts & impulses

correct_answers.text: Forensic assessment of intrusive thoughts & impulses

questions.explanation: The assessment for CBT includes: the context in which OCD has developed; the nature of the obsession(s) – their content, the degree of insight, the frequency of their occurrence, the triggers, the feared consequence, the patient's appraisal of the obsession; the main emotion(s) linked with the obsession or intrusion; the avoidance behaviour; the degree of family involvement and the degree of impact in the person's occupational, social and family life; goals and valued directions in life; readiness to change and expectations of therapy, including previous experience of CBT for the disorder.

questions.question_text: A 36 year-old woman comes into your outpatient clinic. She is obsessed with dirt and contamination, and has to wash her hands up to twenty times if she touches anything. The treatment you would are most likely to recommend would be:
questions.explanation: NICE guidelines on the management of OCD suggest that CBT with exposure and response prevention should be offered to patients with this disorder.

questions.question_text: There is no evidence for which of the following treatments for PTSD?
questions.explanation: Although one four-arm RCT suggested that hypnotherapy reduced intrusive symptoms and avoidance symptom scores significantly, a BMJ clinical evidence review concluded that there was insufficient evidence for the use of hypnotherapy for PTSD.

questions.question_text: A 28 year-old lady with obsessive compulsive disorder is being treated with Sertraline (50 mg) for the last two months. She reports no improvement in her symptoms. The next recommended step would be:
questions.explanation: Sertraline is usually increased up to a maximum of 200 mg/day before the trial is considered to have failed. According to NICE guidelines, after failing a trial of an antidepressant with adequate dosage and duration one should try another SSRI/Clomipramine; if this also fails, combine antidepressant with CBT; if this fails as well, progress to add an antipsychotic.

questions.question_text: When using antidepressants to treat OCD, which ONE of the following may be necessary?
questions.explanation: Usually higher doses are needed for longer times, and relapse on withdrawal is almost inevitable in severe illness.

questions.question_text: The behavioural therapy of agoraphobia includes which ONE of the following?
questions.explanation: Relaxation, graded exposure and desensitisation constitute behavioural therapy for agoraphobia.

questions.question_text: Many anxiety disorders have a gender bias. What is the male:female ratio for Somatization?
questions.explanation: Somatisation is twice more common in women as compared to men.

questions.question_text: Conversion disorder is rarely seen in clinical practice. It is associated with which ONE of the following features?

options.text: Equal tendency for symptoms to present on left and right sides of the body
More symptoms on the left side of the body
More symptoms on the right side of the body

correct_answer.text: More symptoms on the left side of the body

correct_answers.text: More symptoms on the left side of the body

questions.explanation: It has been suggested that conversion symptoms are more common on the left side of the body.

questions.question_text: Dissociative fugue is characterized by which ONE of the following?

options.text: The subject learning a new language
The subject making a purposeful journey
The subject retaining his first name only

correct_answer.text: The subject making a purposeful journey

correct_answers.text: The subject making a purposeful journey

questions.explanation: In fugue, the relocation is different from wandering as it is apparently purposeful.

questions.question_text: Psychiatric patients in medical settings are UNLIKELY to present with which ONE of the following?

options.text: Refusal to accept medical model of illness

correct_answer.text: Refusal to accept medical model of illness

correct_answers.text: Refusal to accept medical model of illness

questions.explanation: Patients seen in medical services who require psychiatric attention are more likely to have presented with somatic than with psychological symptoms; they may present with poor compliance or behaviourally induced medical conditions, or anxiety symptoms—but they do not characteristically refuse to accept the medical model of illness.

questions.question_text: The difference between somatisation and hypochondriasis is:
questions.explanation: Hypochondriasis is the fear of having physical disorder. In somatisation the preoccupation is with the symptoms and not the disorder/diagnosis. Treatment is expected for alleviation of symptoms and not investigation for confirmation of diagnosis.

questions.question_text: A malnourished man who has had numerous admissions to a local general hospital after fainting at public places asks for admission as he is very dizzy. Physical examination was normal. The likely diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: This man is probably homeless and so has a motive in feigning illness, thus qualifying as a malingerer.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following conditions is usually transient and does not have strong evidence-based treatment?
questions.explanation: Reassurance and explanation, antidepressant drugs, exercise and relaxation have all been tried in depersonalisation syndrome. There is however, little in the way of clinical trial evidence to guide treatment.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following in ICD-10 is the diagnosis closest to Chronic Fatigue Syndrome?
questions.explanation: CFS was not recognised when ICD-10 was drafted. Neurasthenia is the code with close agreement.

questions.question_text: What is the motivation behind a factitious disorder?

options.text: Sick role but no monetary gain

correct_answer.text: Sick role but no monetary gain

correct_answers.text: Sick role but no monetary gain

questions.explanation: Illness is feigned for no obvious reason in factitious disorder—they seek the sick role without any external rewards.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is regarded as a medical functional syndrome?
questions.explanation: A population survey found that a large proportion of the community had symptoms such as pain and fatigue without somatic pathology. Functional somatic symptoms—such as fibromyalgia—are common in primary care.

questions.question_text: 'Briquet syndrome' or 'St. Louis hysteria' is an eponym for multiple somatisation disorder. Which ONE of the following is NOT associated with this condition?
questions.explanation: Criteria include a history beginning before the age of 30, multiple physical symptoms, interference with life, repeated physician contact, and lack of any medical explanation. Onset after 40 is not characteristic.

questions.question_text: Suicide is one of the most common causes of death in which ONE of the following groups of patients?
questions.explanation: The national confidential enquiry on maternal death showed the high prevalence of suicide in post-partum women.

questions.question_text: Factors predicting suicide after deliberate self-harm include which ONE of the following?
questions.explanation: Risk factors for suicide include male gender, advancing age, unemployment, concurrent mental disorder, previous attempt, substance abuse, low socioeconomic status, and lack of social support.

questions.question_text: The risk of self harm is increased when which ONE of the following phenomena is noted on mental state examination?
questions.explanation: Command hallucinations to harm oneself are a strong predictor of self-harm.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following neurological illnesses is independently associated with elevated suicide risk, irrespective of depression?
questions.explanation: Individuals with epilepsy have a higher risk of suicide even when controlling for coexisting psychiatric disease.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most common method of attempting suicide in the UK?
questions.explanation: The most commonly used method in suicide attempts by both men and women is self-poisoning. Paracetamol is now the single most common drug used for overdose.

questions.question_text: Deliberate self harm (DSH) is a known risk factor for completed suicide. What is the risk of completed suicide in the year after an episode of DSH?
questions.explanation: Suicide in the general population occurs at about 1 in 10,000 per year; after non-fatal self-harm the incidence rises to around 1 in 100 (0.6–0.9%).

questions.question_text: Anorexia nervosa is suggested to have a genetic basis. The hereditary association is strong for which subtype of the disease?
questions.explanation: Concordance rates for monozygotic twins are higher than dizygotic twins in anorexia nervosa. Restricting anorexia nervosa shows 65% MZ and 32% DZ concordance.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following personality traits is most commonly noted in anorexia patients?
questions.explanation: Anankastic traits are noted in anorexics. High rates of perfectionism are found in non-affected dizygotic twins of anorexia probands.

questions.question_text: The mortality in patients with Anorexia nervosa is higher than in the general population. What is the increased risk of mortality?
questions.explanation: Emborg (1999) calculated a SMR in anorexia of 6.7%. Anorexia is one of the most lethal of psychiatric disorders. It has a 5-10% mortality over ten years. Two-thirds of the deaths are attributable to the direct effects of the disorder and one third are related to suicide.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a component of behavioral therapy used in the treatment of obesity? Choose one answer.
questions.explanation: The simple technique of keeping a diary has been shown to be effective in many cases. The most consistent self-monitors lose more weight than the least consistent self-monitors.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following findings are most likely to be seen in patients with Anorexia Nervosa? Choose one answer.
questions.explanation: The following metabolic and endocrine changes are noted in anorexia: low oestrogen or sex hormones; hypokalemia; high cortisol; leucopenia with relative lymphocytosis; low LHRH, LH, FSH; low oestrogen & progesterone; low T3; high cortisol; high fasting growth harmone levels.

questions.question_text: The babies of anorexic mothers are most likely to be associated with which ONE of the following? Choose one answer.
questions.explanation: A large scale study found that women with Anorexia Nervosa tend to deliver low birth weight babies, though the risk of pre-term birth is similar to controls. Apgar scores were within normal limits. Women with a history of bulimia nervosa (with or without a history of anorexia nervosa) had an increased rate of lifetime miscarriages, as did women with a history of other psychiatric disorders. Foetal loss is more common in anorexic women and they are more likely to require caesarean deliveries. Finally the risk of depression is greater in women with anorexia post partum.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is LEAST commonly associated with Bulimia Nervosa? Choose one answer.
questions.explanation: Oesphagitis, oesophageal tears, dental decay are common in Bullimia, however peptic ulcers are not described in the physical complications of this syndrome. Chest pain occurs secondary to the hypokalemia and is less common, although around 50% of bullmic patients have electrolyte disturbances.

questions.question_text: Family dynamics are often affected for patients with anorexia nervosa. Which ONE of the following features is associated with such problems? Choose one answer.
questions.explanation: Five main characteristics of family interaction were identified as detrimentally linked to anorexic presentation: enmeshment (a tight web of family relationships with the members appearing to read each other's minds), overprotectiveness, rigidity, involvement of the sick child in parental conflicts, lack of resolution of conflicts.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following treatments is the most effective management for chronic fatigue syndrome?
questions.explanation: The mainstay for the treatment of chronic fatigue syndrome is CBT. This involves graded exercise programs, agreed in collaboration with the patient. The cognitive element may look at illness beliefs, patient resistance to engaging in the program, self-esteem etc. The use of antidepressants has conflicting evidence base...

questions.question_text: Delusional parasitosis is often diagnosed by dermatologists. Which ONE of the following substances is associated with it?
questions.explanation: Delusions of parasitosis is the fixed belief that one is infested with living organisms despite a lack of medical evidence of such infestation. Cocaine abuse is associated with tactile hallucinations, described in many cases as crawling, biting, or stinging or other perceptual abnormalities...

questions.question_text: The puerperium is a high-risk period for psychiatric illnesses. The incidence of puerperal psychosis is
questions.explanation: The incidence of puerperal psychosis is variably quoted as 1 in 500 to 1000. This is constant across various cultures.

questions.question_text: Which of the following would be the first-line pharmacological treatment for body dysmorphic disorder?
questions.explanation: Treatment trials have shown that SSRIs or tricyclics with serotonergic rather than noradrenergic properties are the most helpful drugs. NICE guidelines recommend against the use of tricyclics (except clomipramine). They also do not recommend use of MAOIs or SNRIs.

questions.question_text: Individuals with which ONE of the following disorders fake symptoms or disorders as part of a need to maintain the sick role?
questions.explanation: Patients with factitious disorder knowingly fake symptoms, but do so for psychological reasons and not for monetary or other discrete objectives as in the case of Malingering. They usually prefer the sick role and may move from hospital to hospital in order to receive care.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is associated with a psychogenic cause of impotence?
questions.explanation: Emotional factors affecting sex include both interpersonal problems and psychological problems within the individual. In organic sexual dysfunction, masturbation, morning erections are lost, while desire may be preserved in early stages.

questions.question_text: A patient presenting to a plastic surgeon for breast reconstructive surgery most commonly suffers from which ONE of the following?
questions.explanation: Most patients attending clinics for breast reconstruction are post-mastectomy patients. They are free from psychiatric problems more often than not.

questions.question_text: Puerperal depression is most commonly identified by which ONE of the following?
questions.explanation: The majority of depressions occurring at puerperium are mild and do not require specific psychiatric intervention. Most will be uncovered during routine postnatal screening by the general practitioner or health visitor.

questions.question_text: An 80-year old lady is admitted after an 8-month preoccupation with having colon cancer. She’s seen 11 physicians. What is her likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Hypochondriacal disorder is a persistent preoccupation with the possibility of having serious disease. There is a persistent refusal to accept the advice of several different doctors that there is no physical illness underlying the symptoms.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is a direct reason for the neuropsychiatric effects seen in HIV infection?
questions.explanation: HIV causes neuropsychiatric complications by direct effects including encephalitis, cerebral vasculitis, lymphocytic meningitis.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is NOT a feature of chronic fatigue syndrome?

options.text: Feeling tired after rest, relaxation and enjoyment

correct_answer.text: Feeling tired after rest, relaxation and enjoyment

correct_answers.text: Feeling tired after rest, relaxation and enjoyment

questions.explanation: CFS is characterised by fatigue, post-exertional malaise, sleep dysfunction, pain, neurological/cognitive manifestations, autonomic, neuroendocrine and immune manifestations. Feeling tired after normal rest is not a defining feature.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is the most common psychiatric cause of A&E attendance?
questions.explanation: Alcohol misuse is the most common substance misuse disorder. Alcohol problems are encountered particularly frequently in accident and emergency departments.

questions.question_text: A woman in her twenties presents in the A&E with multiple skin rashes and abscesses. After investigations, no cause is found. She has presented many times with various symptoms. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: In factitious disorder repeated doctor seeking occurs without any underlying gain apart from medical attention.

questions.question_text: A 26-year-old man tells his GP he has a severe form of cancer of the nose. He says his regular GP was away and 'didn’t understand' him. What diagnosis best fits?
questions.explanation: This qualifies as a hypochondriacal delusion of body dysmorphic type (persistent delusional disorder).

questions.question_text: A 27-year-old man calls 999 with severe abdominal pain. He’s known to present repeatedly and improves dramatically with parenteral opioids, then walks out demanding more. Diagnosis?
questions.explanation: This is malingering for obtaining opioids.

questions.question_text: During battle a soldier suddenly loses use of his right arm. There are no other neurological signs and he does not appear distressed by his ailment. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The scenario best fits a dissociative (hysterical) motor disorder. The soldier has been subject to psychological trauma and developed paralysis with 'belle indifference.'

questions.question_text: A 45 year old man attends his GP with back pain from a fall at work. Neurological exam yields inconsistent findings. The GP later gets a solicitor’s request for a compensation report. Diagnosis?
questions.explanation: This is most likely to be malingering. Clues include inconsistent symptoms and a clear financial motive.

questions.question_text: A man presents to A+E having wandered far from home. He has no idea what his name is or where he is from. He can register new information and has no impairment of recall. Diagnosis?
questions.explanation: This describes dissociative fugue where the patient wanders far from home with no recollection of personal identity.

questions.question_text: A 40-year-old man was made redundant one week ago. He is depressed, worried about his future, and found abusive towards helpful bank staff. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: This best fits an adjustment disorder, a psychological reaction arising in relation to adapting to new circumstances.

questions.question_text: A 56-year-old man’s secretary committed suicide three months ago. He now has flashbacks, emotional numbing, irritability, and difficulty concentrating. What is the diagnosis?
questions.explanation: There are symptoms congruent with PTSD, including emotional numbing, flashbacks, and irritability.

questions.question_text: A 34-year-old lady in A&E has low mood, palpitations, and tremors the day after her partner suffered a head injury. All investigations are normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: This is an acute stress reaction: immediate, brief psychological response to a sudden, intense stressor.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old housewife presents with over a year of tummy, arm and leg pain and headaches despite normal investigations. She insists on further tests and it’s affecting her relationship. Diagnosis?
questions.explanation: This is somatization disorder—multiple physical complaints for which no physical cause is found.

questions.question_text: A 29-year-old man presents after a brief loss of identity and awareness. He shows repeated stereotyped movements and utterances but his neuro exam is normal. Diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The best fit diagnosis is possession state, where there is temporary loss of personal identity and full awareness.

questions.question_text: A 39-year-old mother is dazed and withdrawn on hearing her daughter has a life-threatening accident, then becomes overactive and irritable shortly afterwards. Diagnosis?
questions.explanation: This is an acute stress reaction: clear precipitant and transient increased arousal.

questions.question_text: A 23-year-old man in A&E with minor injuries becomes anxious, fearful, sweaty and pacing while waiting for tests and self-discharges. He passed out at vaccination. Most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: This is a specific phobia: irrational fear of a specific situation (medical settings), with anticipatory anxiety and avoidance.

questions.question_text: A man complains of tremor, palpitations, dizziness and sweating every time he goes to shops or gets on a bus. He needs his wife with him for errands. Diagnosis?
questions.explanation: This is agoraphobia—a fear of being in public spaces where escape might be difficult, with anticipatory anxiety and avoidance.

questions.question_text: A woman reports intrusive thoughts that she will contaminate her children with germs. She cleans their rooms in a set pattern every morning and won’t let anyone else in. Diagnosis?
questions.explanation: This describes the obsessive thoughts and compulsive rituals seen in OCD.

questions.question_text: A 26-year-old lady lost her mother nine months ago. She now has dizziness, palpitations, nervousness and stomach upset, worse when she travels by car. Diagnosis?
questions.explanation: This describes psychological and somatic symptoms of generalised (‘free-floating’) anxiety.

questions.question_text: A 40-year-old woman referred by her GP cancels two new appointments due to fear of collapsing on the road without help. She worries for days beforehand. Diagnosis?
questions.explanation: This is classic agoraphobia, with fear of leaving the house or traveling and anticipatory anxiety leading to avoidance.

questions.question_text: A 29-year-old student is very low due to inability to find a partner, worries about being alone, lost weight, and fears having hiccups in front of women and embarrassing himself. Diagnosis?
questions.explanation: This describes social phobia: fear of embarrassing oneself in social interactions, leading to avoidance and distress.

questions.question_text: A woman comes to see you in the out-patient clinic. She has a 6 month old son and, for the last three months, has had recurring thoughts of harming him. She does not wish to harm him and these thoughts make her tearful and anxious. The birth was uneventful but she perceives it to have been traumatic. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Although symptoms of depression are the same, the features of anxiety are more common in postnatal depression, and many mothers have fleeting, repetitive and intrusive thoughts about harming the baby. These thoughts are distressing but it is rare for mothers to act on such thoughts.

questions.question_text: Which ONE is TRUE of the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale?

options.text: It is a semi-structured interview conducted by a trainer clinician.
The scale can be used to detect anxiety neuroses, phobias and personality disorder.
It has been shown to be effective as a screening tool.
It is a simple instrument to use with women who cannot read or write.
It is used in secondary mental health services to diagnosis postnatal depression.

correct_answer.text: It has been shown to be effective as a screening tool.

correct_answers.text: It has been shown to be effective as a screening tool.

questions.explanation: The EPDS has been developed to assist primary care health professionals to detect mothers suffering from postnatal depression. The EPDS has been utilized in 23 countries and carries a significant level of sensitivity (86%) and specificity (78%) in identifying those at risk of or potentially suffering from either prenatal or postpartum depression.

questions.question_text: What is the relative risk to the baby of developing Ebstein's anomaly if mother is on lithium in the first trimester of pregnancy?
questions.explanation: The relative risk for congenital defects overall is 7.5, and 10 for Ebstein's anomaly after lithium exposure.

questions.question_text: What is the treatment of choice in a patient with severe symptoms of premenstrual syndrome?
questions.explanation: Research shows SSRIs are very effective in relieving the emotional and physical PMS and PMDD symptoms for most women. SSRI therapy usually brings relief within a few days of starting medication.

questions.question_text: Which of the following antidepressants is expressed in breast milk at the highest concentration?
questions.explanation: Although all psychotropic drugs that have been studied are excreted into breast milk, fluoxetine and citalopram should probably be avoided during lactation as they are found at relatively higher concentrations in breast milk.

questions.question_text: What is the risk of cardiac abnormality in a child born to a mother who was on Lithium in the first trimester of her pregnancy?
questions.explanation: The risk of cardiac abnormality in this situation is 60 per 1000 (6%), compared to 8 per 1000 in the general population.

questions.question_text: You have started a patient with postnatal depression on an antidepressant and wish to monitor changes in her symptoms. Which of the following observer rating scales would you use?
questions.explanation: The Montgomery-Asberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) is an observer-rated depression scale designed to assess and measure the severity of symptoms of depression, including change during treatment.

questions.question_text: A patient with bipolar affective disorder came off her medication during her pregnancy. She delivered four weeks ago and is currently breast feeding her baby. She feels that she may be relapsing and requests medication which is safe for breast feeding. Which ONE of the following would you prescribe?
questions.explanation: NICE Guidelines on Antenatal & Postnatal Mental Health advises use of antipsychotics if medication is required during breast feeding.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following disorders is more common in women than men?
questions.explanation: Psychiatric disorders more common in women include dysthymia, anxiety and phobic disorders, dissociative disorders, eating disorders, and deliberate self-harm.

questions.question_text: Which rating scale would you recommend to screen a health visitor for depression in women after delivery?
questions.explanation: The EPDS is a 10-item self-report scale to screen for postnatal depression in the community.

questions.question_text: Which of the following features are more frequent in the children of mothers suffering from postnatal depression?
questions.explanation: Children of mothers with postnatal depression have demonstrated behavioural problems, frequent insecure attachment, fewer positive facial expressions, more negative facial expressions, and mild cognitive abnormalities.

questions.question_text: What is the incidence of fetal birth defects in a woman taking valproate?
questions.explanation: The risk of fetal birth defects (particularly neural tube defects) in a woman taking sodium valproate is 100–200 per 10,000 (1–2%).

questions.question_text: A young man is impulsive and has angry outbursts. He has been arrested several times for hitting his partner. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Antisocial PD is characterised by any 3 of the following: callous unconcern for the feelings of others; gross and persistent irresponsibility and disregard for social norms; incapacity to maintain enduring relationships; very low tolerance to frustration; incapacity to experience guilt; marked proneness to blame others.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a feature of dissocial personality disorder?

options.text: Lack of desire for confiding relationships

questions.explanation: The ICD-10 criteria for dissocial personality disorder include callous unconcern for the feelings of others and gross and persistent irresponsibility and disregard for social norms, rules and obligations.

questions.question_text: Which of the following did Bateman and Fonagy propose to be effective for borderline personality disorder?
questions.explanation: Partial hospitalisation has been proposed by Bateman and Fonagy (1999) as being more effective for borderline personality disorder than standard psychiatric care.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a criterion for the ICD-10 diagnosis of anxious (avoidant) personality disorder?

options.text: Excessive sensitiveness to setbacks and rebuffs
Feelings of excessive doubt and caution
Preoccupation with being criticised or rejected in social situations
Apparent indifference to praise or criticism

correct_answer.text: Preoccupation with being criticised or rejected in social situations

correct_answers.text: Preoccupation with being criticised or rejected in social situations

questions.explanation: The ICD-10 criteria for anxious (avoidant) PD include a persistent, pervasive tension and apprehension and preoccupation with being criticised or rejected in social situations.

questions.question_text: Anxious (avoidant) and dependent personality disorders are often comorbid with social phobia. Which of the following classes of medication is the most effective treatment for social phobia in this context?
questions.explanation: MAOIs have proven to be efficacious in social phobia comorbid with avoidant and dependent personality disorder.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following personality disorders would be the most appropriate diagnosis in the following case vignette? A 56-year-old single high-school graduate, living alone, who rarely socialises, is adept at fixing things but chooses not to open a shop, appears indifferent to praise, advice or complaints from customers, aloof and barely acknowledges greetings.
questions.explanation: The ICD-10 criteria for schizoid personality disorder include emotional coldness, detachment or flattened affect, limited capacity to express feelings, apparent indifference to praise or criticism, and preference for solitary activities.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true for patients with emotionally unstable personality disorder?

options.text: They are still likely to retain the diagnosis at age 50
They are less likely to have children
They have a normal rate of marriage
They are unlikely to be employed
They have a similar rate of substance misuse

correct_answer.text: They are less likely to have children

correct_answers.text: They are less likely to have children

questions.explanation: Long-term follow-up has shown that odds of having children are one-quarter of the general population, marriage rates are half the average, and only one-quarter fulfil diagnostic criteria at age 50.

questions.question_text: Which of the following medications has been shown to be effective in the management of aggressive behaviour in patients with personality disorder?
questions.explanation: Lithium, valproate and SSRIs have been found to be helpful in the treatment of aggressive and assaultative behaviour.

questions.question_text: What are people with emotionally unstable borderline personality disorder are stuck in?
questions.explanation: The paranoid-schizoid position is characterized by splitting, projective identification, idealization, and omnipotence of thought.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following personality disorders would be the most appropriate diagnosis in the following case vignette? A middle-aged successful businessman requests therapy because 'others have trouble getting on with me.' He has had three marriages, is obsessed with money and power, believes others are weak or incompetent, and has extraordinary confidence in his own ability but is not psychotic or manic.
questions.explanation: Narcissistic PD is characterized by a grandiose sense of self-importance, fantasies of unlimited power or success, belief that one is 'special', need for excessive admiration, sense of entitlement, and interpersonally exploitative behaviour.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following personality disorders would be the most appropriate diagnosis for someone who allows others to make important decisions for them, feels uncomfortable when alone and fears being abandoned?
questions.explanation: The ICD-10 criteria for dependent personality disorder include subordination of own needs to those of others, unwillingness to make demands, discomfort when alone, and fear of being abandoned.

questions.question_text: One of the predictors of negative response to treatment in antisocial personality disorder is:

options.text: Axis 1 diagnosis of organic brain disorder
Axis 1 diagnosis of bipolar affective disorder

correct_answer.text: Axis 1 diagnosis of organic brain disorder

correct_answers.text: Axis 1 diagnosis of organic brain disorder

questions.explanation: Predictors of negative response include a history of arrest for a felony, history of violence, unresolved legal situation, and Axis 1 diagnosis of organic brain impairment.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following personality disorders would be the most appropriate diagnosis in the following case vignette? A 25-year old female junior doctor is reprimanded at work for wearing inappropriate clothing. She always seeks to be the centre of attention and is overly flirtatious. She is occasionally dramatic in displaying emotion.
questions.explanation: Histrionic PD is characterized by self-dramatization, shallow affect, suggestibility, and seeking to be the centre of attention.

questions.question_text: In dissocial personality disorder, which of the following is a predictor of good response to therapy?
questions.explanation: Predictors of good response include presence of anxiety or Axis 1 diagnosis of depression or psychosis.

questions.question_text: A man comes to your out-patient clinic. He gives a history of childhood conduct disorder. He recognises that he has a problem with anger and often gets into fights with his partner. He wishes to prevent this from happening. You interview him and find no evidence of mental illness or active symptoms. What do you decide?

options.text: Start no treatment but review him in three months
Start an antipsychotic and review in 3 months
Start an antidepressant and review in 3 months

questions.explanation: Approaches that reinforce appropriate behaviours and attempt to make connections between the person's actions and their feelings may be more beneficial.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a diagnostic criterion for borderline personality disorder?

options.text: Attempts to avoid real or imagined abandonment

correct_answer.text: Attempts to avoid real or imagined abandonment

correct_answers.text: Attempts to avoid real or imagined abandonment

questions.explanation: DSM and ICD criteria for borderline PD include frantic efforts to avoid real or imagined abandonment.

questions.question_text: Which of the following psychological therapies for personality disorder is an example of 'milieu therapy', in which the social setting itself produces a therapeutic effect?
questions.explanation: Therapeutic communities are a specific example of milieu therapy in which patients live and work together and the social environment is the treatment.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a characteristic finding in patients with personality disorder?

options.text: Less severe symptoms of Axis I psychiatric disorders
Lower rates of Axis I psychiatric disorders
Longer and costlier treatment for Axis I psychiatric disorders
Lower mortality from suicide, accidents and violence
Better prognosis for Axis I psychiatric disorders

correct_answer.text: Longer and costlier treatment for Axis I psychiatric disorders

correct_answers.text: Longer and costlier treatment for Axis I psychiatric disorders

questions.explanation: Common characteristics include high rates of Axis I disorders, more severe symptoms, worse prognosis, longer and costlier treatments, and excess mortality from suicide and accidents.

questions.question_text: In antisocial personality disorder, which of the following is a predictor of positive response to treatment? Choose one answer.

options.text: History of arrest for a felony

questions.explanation: Predictors of positive response to treatment in antisocial personality are the presence of anxiety, Axis 1 diagnosis of depression or Axis 1 diagnosis of psychosis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following has the best evidence of use in pre-menstrual dysphoria?
questions.explanation: Research shows SSRIs are very effective in relieving the emotional and physical PMS and PMDD symptoms for most women. SSRI therapy usually brings relief within a few days of starting medication Selective serotonin-reuptake inhibitors reduce the symptoms of severe premenstrual syndrome. Selective serotonin-reuptake inhibitors reduce the symptoms of severe premenstrual syndrome.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is known to be an effective intervention for premenstrual syndrome?
questions.explanation: The efficacy of SSRIs in the treatment of both physical and psychological symptoms of premenstrual syndrome (Dimmock et al, 2000) has been confirmed and studies have shown that these drugs also reduce functional impairment. The onset of improvement is more rapid than that in SSRI treatment of depressive disorder. Treatment can be given throughout the menstrual cycle, but several studies now support dosing during the luteal phase alone, as this appears to be equally efficacious.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is true for the functional impairment in premenstrual syndrome?

options.text: It is limited to interpersonal relationships.
It causes 20-30% of sufferers to miss work.
It is less severe than that found in dysthymia.
It is greater at home than in work settings.
It is not improved by treatment with SSRIs.

correct_answer.text: It is greater at home than in work settings.

correct_answers.text: It is greater at home than in work settings.

questions.explanation: Pearlstein et al (2000) found that women with premenstrual dysphoric disorder scored worse than women with dysthymia on the parental factor of the Social Adjustment Self Report Scale, a finding consistent with data from a large telephone survey in which symptomatic women reported highest functional impairment at home (Hylan et al, 1999). However, the impairment in occupational function is also significant. In Hylan et al's study, 8-16% of symptomatic women had missed work in the preceding year because of premenstrual syndrome and 5-8% of those who had ever missed work had been absent for more than 14 days in the past year. Even symptomatic women who do not seek treatment for premenstrual syndrome appear to use more healthcare services in general and missed work more often than asymptomatic women.

questions.question_text: Select the TRUE statement regarding dual-role transvestism.

options.text: There is persistent intense distress about assigned sex.
There is a strong desire to join the opposite sex.
Cross-dressing enables individuals to enjoy temporary membership of the opposite sex.
Individuals seek surgical reassignment to the opposite gender.

correct_answer.text: Cross-dressing enables individuals to enjoy temporary membership of the opposite sex.

correct_answers.text: Cross-dressing enables individuals to enjoy temporary membership of the opposite sex.

questions.explanation: Dual-role transvestism includes the wearing of clothes of the opposite sex for part of the time to enjoy a temporary experience of membership of the opposite sex, without the desire for a more permanent sex change. No sexual excitement accompanies this cross-dressing, distinguishing it from fetishistic transvestism.

questions.question_text: A 30-year-old man, dependent on alcohol, comes to the emergency department. He has a wound in his head. He is homeless and becomes agitated while in the department. what the most likely condition he is suffering from if He experiences seeing squirrels crawling over the floor
questions.explanation: The visual hallucinations are most suggestive of delirium tremens.

questions.question_text: A 30-year-old man, dependent on alcohol, comes to the emergency department. He has a wound in his head. He is homeless and becomes agitated while in the department. what the most likely condition he is suffering from if he has 2 abscesses in groin and neck, he has small pupils and is bradycardic.
questions.explanation: These features are suggestive of opiate overdose intoxication.

questions.question_text: A 30-year-old man, dependent on alcohol, comes to the emergency department. He has a wound in his head. He is homeless and becomes agitated while in the department. what the most likely condition he is suffering from if he doesn‘t recognise the left side of his body.
questions.explanation: This hemi-neglect is most likely to have been caused by an intracranial bleed.

questions.question_text: A 23-year-old woman in the first trimester of pregnancy develops agitation, paranoid ideation and third person auditory hallucinations. Her appetite, energy and sleep are all normal. what  is the most appropriate wtreatment. Assume that the benefits of pharmacology outweigh the disadvantages.
questions.explanation: Trifluoperazine and chlorpromazine are the agents whose use has been most reported in pregnancy. Both olanzapine and clozapine appear to be relatively safe, but experience with their use is more limited.

questions.question_text: A 31-year-old woman in the second trimester of pregnancy develops low mood, hopelessness and suicidal ideation. Her appetite, energy and sleep are all reduced.  what  is the most appropriate wtreatment. Assume that the benefits of pharmacology outweigh the disadvantages.
questions.explanation: While most experience is with tricyclics such as nortriptyline, amitriptyline and imipramine, there is a reasonable amount of evidence suggesting that fluoxetine is relatively safe.

questions.question_text: A 31-year-old woman who is breast-feeding her one-month-old infant develops low mood, hopelessness and suicidal ideation. Her appetite, energy and sleep are all reduced.  what  is the most appropriate wtreatment. Assume that the benefits of pharmacology outweigh the disadvantages.
questions.explanation: While both paroxetine and sertraline are excreted into breast milk, infant levels of these drugs have been shown to be very low, and so they are probably safe to give to the breast-feeding mother. Infant serum levels of fluoxetine tend to be a little higher in this situation.

questions.question_text: A 27-year-old woman who is breast-feeding her two-month-old infant develops severe sleep disturbance but has no other symptoms of psychiatric illness.  what  is the most appropriate wtreatment. Assume that the benefits of pharmacology outweigh the disadvantages.
questions.explanation: Zolpidem is to be preferred over zopiclone as there is more evidence to suggest that excreted amounts are minimal with no observed effects on nursed infants.

questions.question_text: A 32-year-old opiate dependent woman in the second trimester of her pregnancy wants to stop using heroin but is scared of withdrawal symptoms. select the most likely treatment
questions.explanation: Methadone is the only medication currently licensed for use in opioid detox or substitution treatment in pregnancy.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old man has recently finished detoxification from opioids. He is very motivated to stop using any heroin, and seeks treatment to help him stop opioid use, but is not keen on any substitution treatment. select the most likely treatment
questions.explanation: Naltrexone, an opioid antagonist, has been used to prevent relapses in people who have completed detox and don’t want to be on substitution treatment.

questions.question_text: A 22-year-old man who was recently started on outpatient methadone treatment is found unconscious. He is tachycardic and has pinpoint pupils on examination. select the most likely treatment
questions.explanation: Naloxone reverses the effects of heroin.

questions.question_text: A 78-year-old gentleman, diagnosed to have depression, was started on Sertraline. A few days later he was found to have muscle weakness and drowsiness. Choose ONE metabolic abnormality
questions.explanation: Hyponatremia, a side effect with SSRIs and Carbamazepine, leads to confusion, drowsiness, muscle weakness, and seizures.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old man with history of alcohol dependence went on a drinking spree on a Friday night. He was found to be anxious, sweating profusely and confused by the next morning. Choose ONE metabolic abnormality.
questions.explanation: Hypoglycaemia, due to prolonged drinking and not eating adequately, is frequently encountered in patients with alcohol binges.

questions.question_text: A 40-year-old man, with a diagnosis of resistant schizophrenia, was started on clozapine. Three weeks later he was found to be confused. His carers mentioned that he was complaining of tiredness, increased thirst and increased urinary frequency. Choose ONE metabolic abnormality.
questions.explanation: Clozapine-induced hyperglycaemia; part of the metabolic syndrome, is being tested.

questions.question_text: A woman with bipolar disorder on lithium attending pre-conceptual counselling.
questions.explanation: Lithium is associated with the congenital malformation Ebstein‘s anomaly, which is abnormality of tricuspid valve, wherein there could be an abnormal attachment of one or two leaflets of the tricuspid valve.

questions.question_text: A pregnant woman taking sodium valproate for her epilepsy.
questions.explanation: Sodium valproate is associated with neural tube defects (2-8%). It is also associated with craniofacial abnormalities.

questions.question_text: A woman on diazepam for her anxiety disorder has discovered that she is pregnant.
questions.explanation: Benzodiazepines given in the first trimester is associated with oral cleft.

questions.question_text: An 18-year-old man presents with a two month history of panic attacks, anxiety and vivid flashbacks. He has recently become more withdrawn, and at times shown inappropriate behaviour. On examination he has a conjunctival injection and a cough. diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Social withdrawal, change of behaviour, respiratory symptoms and red eyes are suggestive of cannabis use.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old man of no fixed abode is an inpatient on the medical ward. The nursing staff state he is confused and disorientated. He has been observed shouting and picking up invisible objects off the floor. At times he appears terrified and is talking to imaginary people by his bed. He is restless, tremulous and hypertensive. diagnosis?
questions.explanation: This acute confusion and visual hallucinations in a dishevelled man are suggestive of delirium tremens.

questions.question_text: A 19-year-old man with a history of polysubstance abuse, is sweating profusely, appears to be agitated and tachycardic. He claims to see the colour red while listening to his CDs. diagnosis
questions.explanation: The physiological arousal and synaesthetic features suggest LSD use.

questions.question_text: A young girl with history of childhood sexual abuse, who has chronic suicidal ideation which she often expresses by episodes of deliberate self-harm. She gets cross with some nurses who are treating her. Choose ONE of the personality disorders.
questions.explanation: This describes borderline personality disorder.

questions.question_text: A man with illusions, obsessive ruminations and suspiciousness, does not socialize properly and has poor relations with people. He had an avid interest in studying psychology, and tends to like collecting pebbles with a particular grain on them. There is no history of hallucinations. Choose ONE of the personality disorders.
questions.explanation: This describes features of schizotypal disorder.

questions.question_text: A university student who gets angry and says on failing his thesis, "they are all jealous of me and seem to be irritating me purposefully". His family says he is always mistrusting of people, and of a complaining nature. Choose ONE of the personality disorders.
questions.explanation: This describes features of paranoid personality disorder.

questions.question_text: A woman is kept waiting for a couple of minutes by her CPN, who had to take a telephone call. She smashes the nearby window and threatens to slash her wrists. She appears to have made similar threats in the past. Choose ONE of the personality disorders.
questions.explanation: The impulsive behaviour and threats of self-harm suggest emotionally unstable: impulsive personality disorder.

questions.question_text: A 28-year-old man has written a detailed complaint to the Chief Executive of the trust owing to ill treatment by all the health professionals involved in his care. He was being treated for delusional disorder, jealous type. Choose ONE of the personality disorders.
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is paranoid personality disorder, whose members tend to be resentful, self-important and bear grudges.

questions.question_text: A 37-year-old charming man is seen in the outpatients for his alcohol dependence. He has a long forensic history, which he forgets to mention. When the doctor questions him about this, he says that most of the offences were due to the fault of others. Choose ONE of the personality disorders.
questions.explanation: This is dissocial PD who do not adhere to social norms, fail to take responsibility for their actions and display superficial charm.

questions.question_text: A 20-year-old man is brought to casualty in the early hours of the morning after suddenly developing the belief that his friends are conspiring to kill him. His pupils are dilated and he is sweating, agitated and tachycardic.
questions.explanation: People intoxicated with amphetamines can develop acute psychotic episodes, which are relatively short-lived. Another clue to the diagnosis is the characteristic physical symptoms.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old man of no fixed abode is an inpatient on the medical ward. The nursing staff states that he is confused and disorientated. He has been observed shouting and picking up invisible objects off the floor. At times he appears terrified and is talking to imaginary people by his bed. He is restless, tremulous and hypertensive.
questions.explanation: Delirium tremens best fits this clinical picture. The core features are all present, including: clouding of consciousness, bizarre affect, hallucinations, autonomic disturbance and tremor. 3. The clinical picture is one of opiate withdrawal. The woman will not have had access to drugs while in custody and has developed withdrawal symptoms. Another clue is that she has been arrested for shoplifting, which may be to finance her addiction.

questions.question_text: A young woman has been brought to casualty by the police, having been arrested for shoplifting. While in custody she became unwell, complaining of severe abdominal cramps and pain in her muscles and joints. In the casualty department she appears restless; she is sweating profusely and has ‗goose bumps‘ on her skin.
questions.explanation: The clinical picture is one of opiate withdrawal. The woman will not have had access to drugs while in custody and has developed withdrawal symptoms. Another clue is that she has been arrested for shoplifting, which may be to finance her addiction.

questions.question_text: Even though this selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) is excreted in the breast milk, it is detected in infants‘ serum in low levels and no adverse effects have been reported.
questions.explanation: From case reports, citalopram was associated with uneasy sleep in an infant and fluoxetine use caused adverse effects in two infants.

questions.question_text: No adverse side-effects have been reported with this tricyclic antidepressant in infants who were exposed to it by breast-feeding.
questions.explanation: Doxepin caused reversible adverse effects in two infants.

questions.question_text: This antipsychotic has improved lactation in lactating mothers and no adverse effects were noted in the nursing infants.
questions.explanation: Some studies reported lethargy in infants whose mothers were on chlorpromazine.

questions.question_text: This benzodiazepine is recommended for breast-feeding mothers.
questions.explanation: Long-acting benzodiazepines cause lethargy, sedation and weight loss in infants.
